profile.headline: Staff Software Engineer
profile.summary:
My education and experience have been both technical and people focused, and that reflects who I am. I'm committed to a people-centered approach to software management. That's essential for a healthy engineering team, one that's not only productive but happy as well. We have to deliver results, but we also have to enjoy the journey. They counterbalance each other.

Some of my guiding principles on management:

1. Unleash the natural talent and energy of your team.
        • Software development is a human endeavor, so it's as much social as technical.
        • Happiness, productivity, and sustainability all support each other.
        • Encourage collaboration and creativity by fostering a culture of trust, friendship, humor, and candor.
        • Create work processes that foster trust, responsibility, collaboration, and creative freedom.
        • People are not machines. Their contributions and energy will naturally wax and wane.
        • Observe, ask questions, and listen. Discover what motivates/demotivates each member of your team.
        • Budget time for your team to learn and "play" with new ideas. It's essential for a healthy engineering ecosystem. You're fertilizing the soil for future growth.
        • Remember that your team is on the "makers" schedule not the "managers" schedule (http://www.paulgraham.com/makersschedule.html).
2. Provide focus, direction, and clarity.
        • Provide clear goals, but allow the team to creatively discover the best path(s) to reach them.
3. Manage expectations to deliver results at a sustainable pace.

Some of my guiding principles on collaboration:

1. The goal is to arrive at someplace better together.
2. Candor, humor, and half-baked ideas are not only welcome but expected.
3. Making the effort to understand a colleague's idea, identifying its strengths before looking for its weaknesses, is as important and creative as offering your own.

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer
positions.description: I work on Mozilla's support website (https://support.mozilla.org).
positions.insights: Skills: SQL · Kubernetes · Docker · Django · Python (Programming Language)

positions.title: Software Engineering Manager
positions.description: I manage the MDN Web Docs engineering team, a group of Node, Python, and front-end developers from across the world (Germany, US East Coast, South Africa) focused on making the MDN Web Docs platform world-class. I'm also still responsible for most of our Kubernetes and AWS infrastructure, including for example our AWS EKS, CloudFront, and Lambda@Edge instances, with help from the IT-based SRE team.

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer
positions.description:
I helped architect and move MDN Web Docs from a Django/RDS-based service to a JAMStack (https://jamstack.org/) approach. Our API service is Python/Django/MySQL running in an EKS-based Kubernetes cluster, while our document build-and-deploy (to S3 behind CloudFront) code is Node/React and runs on a daily basis via GitHub actions.

I wrote the "Simplified back-end platform" section of the "MDN Web Docs evolves!" Hacks blog post (https://hacks.mozilla.org/2020/10/mdn-web-docs-evolves-lowdown-on-the-upcoming-new-platform/), which describes all of this in more detail.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer (Backend)
positions.description:
I'm a core developer on the MDN Web Docs (https://developer.mozilla.org/) team. My focus is on backend development using a technology stack that includes Python, Django, MySQL, Celery, Redis, Node.js, Express, AWS (EKS, RDS, CloudFront, ElasticCache, Route53, S3, ELB, Lambda, Lambda@Edge, IAM, etc.), Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Sentry, and New Relic.

Some highlights of my work over the past few years:
* Co-lead the transition of the entire MDN Web Docs infrastructure out of the corporate data center into AWS and Kubernetes, which included defining all of our Kubernetes resources.
* Responsible for moving MDN Web Docs behind a CDN.
* Developed much of the Jenkins-based CI/CD pipeline, including building and registering Docker images, running tests, and deploying to our Kubernetes cluster.
* Created the initial testing framework and tests for our document macros.

Nearly all of my work has been in the open within the following GitHub repositories:
* https://github.com/mdn/kuma
* https://github.com/mdn/kumascript
* https://github.com/mdn/infra
* https://github.com/mdn/yari

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
I created and supported RESTful API's using a technology stack that included Python, HAProxy, nginx, gunicorn, Flask, SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL, marshmallow, pytest, tox, git, Gemfury, Stash, Bamboo, and Trello.

* Led development for the high-volume posting API project, a RESTful interface for publishing and managing job listings on the Idealist.org website, including project estimation, working with product management on feature refinement, creating engineering documentation, steering the architecture of the implementation, creating tests that provided 100% line coverage, and leading the software development team.

* Created a prototype of the high-volume posting API (for early adopter feedback) within AWS using API Gateway, Lambda, Python, boto3, and DynamoDB.

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description:
I worked within the Bioinformatics team, where my focus was split between DevOps and application development, using a technology stack which included Ansible, React, nginx, uWSGI, gevent, Flask, SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL, click, pytest, tox, git, git-flow, Splunk, GitHub, and Travis-CI.

*  Initiated and led the effort to define, create, and support the entire Ansible-based deployment system, working closely with IT as well as the developers.

* I worked closely with scientists to understand and automate their information-tracking tasks, creating and supporting REST API's for web applications, working with front-end developers, and creating application deployment scripts using Ansible. These applications were essential for creating fast turn-around times on production orders.

* Initiated and led the effort to move away from a single, monolithic code repo to a modular, version-able, pip-installable, package-based system.

* Enjoyed mentoring team members who were less-experienced in Python.

* Initiated and led the effort to use GitHub and Travis-CI instead of Atlassian's Stash and Bamboo, including transferring repos and configuring the Travis-CI builds.

positions.title: Senior Python Developer
positions.description:
I worked within the Information Systems group, which was responsible for movie-related production tracking and related infrastructure. The technology stack I used included Python, Twisted, nginx, Cyclone/Tornado, Flask, Redis, MongoDB, Oracle, PostgreSQL, SQLAlchemy, Celery, Apache Solr, memcached, PyGTK, PyQt, pytest, tox, Twisted's trial, Selenium, some AWS products (EC2, S3, SQS, Cloud Formation, etc.), as well as JavaScript, jQuery, HTML and CSS.

* I was the lead developer for Industrial Light & Magic's global system of web and desktop tools centered around the creation and tracking of reviews of takes for shots. This system of tools was critical to the daily operation of ILM, comprising web services, web applications, PyGTK applications with embedded WebKit views, and command-line applications. As part of this ongoing effort, I worked with project managers, developers, ATD's, digital production supervisors, and VFX supervisors across the globe.

* Initiated and created a new multi-site, "reviews" web service built on an asynchronous web framework (Cyclone, Twisted) that was much faster, more efficient, and more reliable than the service it replaced.

* Initiated and led a project to create a new reviews-subscription service called Audience that allowed artists, producers, and VFX supervisors to easily subscribe to only the review threads they were interested in, based on a range of criteria like show, sequence, shot, artist discipline, and location.

* Led the technical effort of a small team to create a new take management tool for dailies, guiding and mentoring junior members.

* I also contributed-to and supported fundamental infrastructure like our distributed task queue, our global pub/sub system, and our global database pool services.

positions.title: Development Principal Engineer (Software)
positions.description: Sole software engineer for a group of about 80 scientists and engineers from all over the world within an R&D group called the Alternative Technology Group. I used Python and its eco-system (Twisted, matplotlib, NumPy, etc.) to develop solutions that automated the extraction, analysis, and visualization of test data, reducing the cycle-of-learning time on experiments.

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description: I used Python (and some Tcl) on Linux/Solaris/AIX to create internal tools that improved R&D work flows, created and managed the installations of open-source (Python, Tcl) and commercial applications, managed and customized a version and configuration management system used by the IC design group (DesignSync), and created documentation that ensured compliance with FDA and other regulations.

positions.title: Co-Founder & Lead Developer
positions.description:
This is a company I helped co-found with two other colleagues.

* Co-architected and created a commercial-quality, cross-platform EDA application using C/C++, the Qt GUI framework, STLport (www.STLport.org), a third-­party package for schematic viewing (www.concept.de), embedded Python and Tcl interpreters, and the OpenAccess IC design database (C++ API) (openeda.si2.org).

* Created a set of C++ classes for parsing using a recursive-descent approach (similar to Boost's “spirit” library), and used these classes to create Verilog <> OpenAccess translators which ran roughly 2X faster than the official Si2 Lex/Yacc-based translators.

positions.title: Lead Architect/Principal Development Engineer
positions.description:
* Led a team in designing an architecture for the Field Programmable Object-Array (FPOA) product comprising a set of custom processors, their communication scheme, and their programming model. I led team meetings, resolved technical (as well as relational) disputes, and interviewed and recommended candidates that were hired as part of the team.

* Shared in the FPOA patent application #20040130346 (see below).

* Developed a Python-based tool that created a synthesizable Verilog RTL model of the FPOA based on architectural-level parameters (e.g., the size of the array, bus-sizes).

* Created a coder/decoder for multi-level signal communication (patent application #20030152154 -- see below) using a constraint-driven tool to find and rank all possible solutions and generate a synthesizable Verilog RTL model of the best solution.

positions.title: Lead Software Engineer
positions.description: We didn't make much money, but we had a lot of fun!  I created a Windows application for cabinet makers (with 2D/3D views) using   C/C++ and MFC.  The GUI design was noted by product reviewers for its power and simplicity.  I also presented and demonstrated the product at trade shows.

positions.title: Senior Applications Engineer
positions.description:
Started my career as a digital hardware engineer within the Fault Evaluator (FE) team at Zycad, a successful startup within the electronic design automation (EDA) market.  The FE was a fault simulation supercomputer used to accelerate the generation of high-quality test vectors for digital systems.  Developed a comprehensive technical training program that detailed the algorithm and architecture of the FE product for current and incoming team members.

After a brief stint at Floating Point Systems, where I helped design the control unit for the CPU of a new mini-supercomputer product, I returned to Zycad as a Senior Applications Engineer, assuming the lead role in technical support for the FE product.  Provided remote and on-site pre/post-sales technical support for our field application engineers as well as key national and international accounts such as the National Security Agency (NSA), IBM, Siemens, and Marubeni Hytech (our Japanese distributor).

educations.fieldOfStudy: Electrical Engineering with Computer Engineering Emphasis

projects.title: txpool
projects.description: A persistent process pool in Python for use with Twisted. Twisted is a Python-based event-driven networking engine for doing asynchronous I/O.

projects.title: walnut (unfinished)
projects.description:
A cross-process/cross-host Redis-based memoizing decorator in Python for asynchronous
(and sycnhronous) functions in Twisted applications (http://twistedmatrix.com).

patents.title: Silicon object array with unidirectional segmented bus architecture
patents.description: A logic array is provided, which includes a plurality of unidirectional segmented buses connecting a plurality of processing elements, called silicon objects, within an integrated circuit. The bus includes a string of unidirectional bus segments. Each silicon object includes a bus input coupled to one of the bus segments in the first bus, and a bus output coupled to a next subsequent one of the bus segments in the first bus. A landing circuit is coupled to the bus input for receiving digital information from the bus input. A function-specific logic block is coupled to an output of the landing circuit and has a result output. Each silicon object further includes a multiplexer having first and second inputs coupled to the bus input and the result output, respectively, and having an output coupled to the bus output.

patents.title: Coding and decoding system and method for high-speed data transmission
patents.description: This document discusses high speed data communication systems and methods, such as for communicating symbols using pulse-amplitude-modulated (PAM) or other multilevel (i.e., more than two) signal levels (e.g., PAM5 symbols using five signal levels). One example encodes and/or decodes between n-bit blocks of binary data (e.g., n=12) and m-symbol code words (e.g., m=6 PAM5 symbols). In this example, the code words are selected to limit the runlength of consecutive symbols transmitted without a symmetric-about-baseline transition between signal levels. In another example, the code words bound a word disparity representing a cumulative deviation from baseline of the values of the symbols of the code words. In a further example, the code words bound an intraword disparity representing a symbol-by-symbol cumulative deviation from baseline, within the code word. Symmetric code words with the same amount, but opposite signs, of nonzero word disparity are paired and together mapped to a unique code of the n-bit block of binary data. During communication, a running disparity is computed, and the code word of the pair that will reduce the running disparity is communicated. Word boundaries are discerned by communicating a nondata control word. In one example, the code or control words are selected to improve immunity to single symbol transmission error. In another example, error checking is performed using the word and running disparities.

I used Python and its eco-system (Twisted, matplotlib, NumPy, etc.) to develop solutions that automated the extraction, analysis, and visualization of test data, reducing the cycle-of-learning time on experiments.

experience.title: Principal Software Engineer
experience.description: I used Python (and some Tcl) on Linux/Solaris/AIX to create internal tools that improved R&D work flows, created and managed the installations of open-source (Python, Tcl) and commercial applications, managed and customized a version and configuration management system used by the IC design group (DesignSync), and created documentation that ensured compliance with FDA and other regulations.

experience.title: Co-Founder & Lead Developer
experience.description:
This is a company I helped co-found with two other colleagues.

* Co-architected and created a commercial-quality, cross-platform EDA application using C/C++, the Qt GUI framework, STLport (www.STLport.org), a third-­party package for schematic viewing (www.concept.de), embedded Python and Tcl interpreters, and the OpenAccess IC design database (C++ API) (openeda.si2.org).

* Created a set of C++ classes for parsing using a recursive-descent approach (similar to Boost's “spirit” library), and used these classes to create Verilog <> OpenAccess translators which ran roughly 2X faster than the official Si2 Lex/Yacc-based translators.

experience.title: Lead Architect/Principal Development Engineer
experience.description:
* Led a team in designing an architecture for the Field Programmable Object-Array (FPOA) product comprising a set of custom processors, their communication scheme, and their programming model. I led team meetings, resolved technical (as well as relational) disputes, and interviewed and recommended candidates that were hired as part of the team.

* Shared in the FPOA patent application #20040130346 (see below).

* Developed a Python-based tool that created a synthesizable Verilog RTL model of the FPOA based on architectural-level parameters (e.g., the size of the array, bus-sizes).

* Created a coder/decoder for multi-level signal communication (patent application #20030152154 -- see below) using a constraint-driven tool to find and rank all possible solutions and generate a synthesizable Verilog RTL model of the best solution.

experience.title: Lead Software Engineer
experience.description: We didn't make much money, but we had a lot of fun!  I created a Windows application for cabinet makers (with 2D/3D views) using   C/C++ and MFC.  The GUI design was noted by product reviewers for its power and simplicity.  I also presented and demonstrated the product at trade shows.

experience.title: Senior Applications Engineer
experience.description:
Started my career as a digital hardware engineer within the Fault Evaluator (FE) team at Zycad, a successful startup within the electronic design automation (EDA) market.  The FE was a fault simulation supercomputer used to accelerate the generation of high-quality test vectors for digital systems.  Developed a comprehensive technical training program that detailed the algorithm and architecture of the FE product for current and incoming team members.

After a brief stint at Floating Point Systems, where I helped design the control unit for the CPU of a new mini-supercomputer product, I returned to Zycad as a Senior Applications Engineer, assuming the lead role in technical support for the FE product.  Provided remote and on-site pre/post-sales technical support for our field application engineers as well as key national and international accounts such as the National Security Agency (NSA), IBM, Siemens, and Marubeni Hytech (our Japanese distributor).
